notes: Hand-picked from the species the South Africa trip does not hold, for the arid west and north: the Karoo (Karoo National Park, Tankwa, Namaqualand, the Richtersveld edge), Upington and the Orange River, the Kgalagadi and Kalahari thornveld (Kuruman, Witsand) and the Northern Cape larks. The country trip already has most of the headline birds of this region (Karoo, Familiar and Southern Anteater-Chat, Namaqua Sandgrouse, Pygmy Falcon, Sociable Weaver, Kalahari Scrub Robin, Karoo and Black Bustard, Ludwig's Bustard, Karoo Lark), so this pack holds what is left: nine larks and sparrow-larks, korhaans and sandgrouse, a courser, and the small birds of scrub and thornveld. The rank was GBIF/eBird record counts (za/occurrence.csv) plus birding knowledge. Left out: Barlow's Lark and Northern Black Korhaan under that name (Barlow's Lark is not in the database; White-quilled Bustard is the Northern Black Korhaan), vagrants, Dune Lark (Namib only), Namibian birds. Birds that fit here but sit in another South Africa pack: Gabar Goshawk, Swallow-tailed Bee-eater, Southern White-faced and Verreaux's Eagle-Owl, Rufous-cheeked and Freckled Nightjar, Double-banded Sandgrouse and Courser, Temminck's Courser, Red-necked Falcon, Lesser Grey Shrike, Abdim's Stork, Ashy Tit, Black-chested Prinia, Black-faced Waxbill, Cut-throat and Mouse-coloured Sunbird (Kruger and the Lowveld), Yellow-bellied Eremomela and Barred Wren-Warbler (KwaZulu-Natal), Alpine Swift and Lesser Kestrel (Fynbos). Black-throated Canary and Cinnamon-breasted Warbler are in the Lowveld pack's scope too; they belong here (arid west) and the Lowveld pack should drop them. Left out for lack of usable photos in the library: White-backed Mousebird (whbmou1, only one trustworthy photo) and Tractrac Chat (tracha1, ten photos in the library and only one usable). Add them back when reviewed photos exist.
